summary: Integrated arity/compression indexing, spectral-vs-chronological separation, multimodal synchronous-state harmonics, projection-bounded inference, covariance/cycle-consistency tests, and relay registry bindings.

First crosswise pass: separated medium from encoding logic; identified Ugarit as decisive dual-script control; added ancient crosswalk calibration, concordant redundancy, transformation covariance, cycle consistency and divergence-gradient tests; preserved spectral-vs-chronological distinction.
key_findings: Egyptian and cuneiform independently increase phonetic explicitness as writing takes on broader linguistic burden.
Ugarit holds material technology relatively constant while changing encoding granularity.
Root arity and sign arity must remain independent.
Indo-European root enlargement provides an independent mechanism control, not proof of Semitic derivation.
Ancient scribal crosswalks should calibrate uncertain transformations before speculative projection.

summary: Added Rosetta Nexus parallax calibration: multilingual stelae/tablets/monuments are now first-class calibration objects with representation-distance levels, alignment granularity, carrier geometry, anchors, transform vectors, covariance, cycle consistency, divergence and residue variables.
invariants: parallax depth is representation distance, not confidence
same object does not imply literal translation
same event does not imply same lexicalization
explicit ancient crosswalks outrank retrospective resemblance for calibration
